chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Ishaq ibn Ja'far, from his father عليه السلام, who said:
It was said to him, "They claim that Abu Talib was a disbeliever." So he said, "They have lied. How could he be a disbeliever while he was saying:"
"Do you not know that we found Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم a Prophet, like Musa عليه السلام, written in the earliest books?"
And in another hadith: "How could Abu Talib be a disbeliever while he was saying:"

"They certainly know that our son is not deemed a liar by us, nor is heed paid to the speech of falsehood against him; and [he is] fair-faced, by whose face the clouds are asked for rain, a refuge for the orphans, a protection for the widows."

key_terms.كَافِرًا: a disbeliever; one who rejects faith
key_terms.نَبِيًّا: a Prophet; one divinely appointed to convey God's message

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show that Abu Talib was not a disbeliever?
ai.summary: This hadith rejects the claim that Abu Talib was a disbeliever by citing his own verses affirming the Prophethood of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. The report presents Abu Talib as one who recognized the truth of the Messenger and praised his noble rank and blessed presence.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Bakr Bin Muhammad Al Azady, 
(It has been narrated) from Is’haq son of Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, from his father<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, said, ‘It was said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘They (people) are claiming that Abu Talib<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">ws</sup> was a disbeliever’. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">ws</sup> said: ‘They are lying! How can he<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">ws</sup> happen to be a disbeliever and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">ws</sup> was saying: ‘Are you not knowing that we<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">ws</sup> found Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> as a Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup><sup style="font-weight: normal">ws</sup> like Musa<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, written in the former Books?’.

And in another Hadeeth – ‘How can Abu Talib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> happen to be a disbeliever and he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> was saying (in prose): ‘They (people) have know that our<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> son<sup>saww</sup> neither lies from us<sup>asws</sup>, nor can he<sup>saww</sup> be faulted with the words of falsehood, and he<sup>saww</sup> is white, the clouds quench by his<sup>saww</sup> face, a protector of the orphans and chastity of the widows’.
en.sarwar: 28. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“The case of abu Talib islike the case of the people of the cave who hid their faith and expressed polytheism.
Allah gave them twice as much reward.”
